sections.title: Defining the Problem: Can we fit a square inside a closed loop?
lecture_lines: Can we fit a square inside any loop?
animations: Superimpose a square onto the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blob.svg] in #FFFF00. Label 'Square' in #FFFFFF.
Show the vertices of the square trying to fit the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blob.svg] in #FF0000.

sections.title: The Topological Mapping: Circles to Squares
animations: Represent the loop as points on a circle in #00FF00. Label 'Circle'. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Define a mapping from circle points to square corners in #FF00FF. Label 'Mapping'.
Highlight the relationship between circle and square vertices using lines in #FFFFFF.
Show the function f(x) for points on the circle in #FF0000.
Connect the circle points to the square edges visually in #FFFF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Applying the Topology: Why it works
lecture_lines: Mismatch functions must pass through zero.
animations: Show the function f(x) as defined previously in #FFFFFF, accompanied by a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] to guide the viewer.
Identify antipodal points on the circle as x and -x in #00FFFF.
Animate f(x) and f(-x) meeting the topological conditions in #FF00FF.
Highlight the crossing point that implies a solution exists in #00FF00.
Conclude that a square must exist on the loop in #FFFF00, with a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] confirming the result.
